articles.title: Assessing Rule Adherence of LLM Adjudicators in Call of Cthulhu TRPG
articles.summary: The paper introduces CoC-Seduce, an adversarial benchmark testing whether LLMs acting as rule adjudicators in Call of Cthulhu can resist user attempts to bypass explicit game rules through rhetorical framing. Across 22 target models and 5,376 adversarial samples, the authors find that newer models and explicit reasoning do not reliably improve robustness, with pseudo-logical framing proving especially effective.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a narrow technical benchmark, but it highlights a broader governance issue for AI agents: models can be manipulated when user intent conflicts with system rules. For advisor conversations, the read-through is that enterprise AI adoption will require stronger controls, testing, and validation before autonomous systems are trusted in regulated or rules-based workflows.

articles.title: Can an Open Model Do Security Research? Cantina’s apex-flash-1 Solves 40 of 60 Held-Out Bug Tasks
articles.summary: Cantina Security and Yeta Labs released apex-flash-1, an open-weights AI model designed for vulnerability research. The model is a reinforcement learning fine-tune of Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash, available on Hugging Face under an MIT license, and reportedly solved 40 of 60 held-out bug tasks. Deployment is possible through vLLM, SGLang, or Transformers, but BF16 operation requires roughly 640 GB of GPU memory.
articles.advisor_relevance: This highlights continued specialization of AI models for high-value enterprise workflows such as cybersecurity research. The large GPU memory requirement also reinforces that advanced open models may still drive demand for substantial AI infrastructure even when model weights are freely available.

articles.title: Network-in-the-Loop at Scale: GPU-Batched 5G Simulation for Massively Parallel Robot Learning
articles.summary: The paper introduces Isaac-Net, an open-source GPU-batched 5G New Radio simulation module designed to keep network behavior inside massively parallel robot-learning loops. It aims to improve realism versus simplified independent-delay models while scaling to about one million simulated robots on one GPU at 83% of the Isaac Lab rate without the network.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early technical development rather than a commercial deployment, but it highlights the growing infrastructure needs around physical AI, robotics, private 5G, and high-fidelity simulation. It may be relevant as a signal that advanced robot training increasingly depends on GPU-accelerated simulation of real-world constraints such as network latency and traffic contention.
